search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting West Nile virus human cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and case classifications for California during August 2024 (2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31), covering state-level and county-level data across official public health agencies, surveillance databases, and news/situation reports.
search_reasoning: West Nile virus in California is primarily reported through the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) and the California West Nile Virus website (westnile.ca.gov), which publish weekly surveillance summaries including human case counts by county, neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive classification, deaths, and cumulative totals. The CDC ArboNET system also aggregates state-reported WNV data. County-level health departments (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno) may issue their own press releases or situation reports. News outlets frequently cite CDPH figures during peak season (July–September). The upstream queries are overly reliant on exact-phrase matching with date-range strings embedded in the query text, which is unlikely to match real page content. This iteration replaces them with cleaner, more realistic queries targeting the known reporting structure: CDPH weekly WNV summaries, the westnile.ca.gov surveillance dashboard, CDC ArboNET, and news coverage. Given the 4-query cap per iteration and 2-iteration max, priority is given to the highest-yield source types: (1) CDPH/westnile.ca.gov official surveillance, (2) CDC ArboNET national database, (3) county health department reports, and (4) news coverage citing official figures. Literature (peer-reviewed) is deprioritized for this narrow 1-month window as publication lag makes 2024 papers unlikely. The language is English only; no localization needed for California.

query_batch.query: West Nile virus California 2024 human cases deaths weekly report site:westnile.ca.gov OR site:cdph.ca.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: The California West Nile Virus website (westnile.ca.gov) and CDPH (cdph.ca.gov) are the primary authoritative sources for weekly WNV human surveillance summaries in California. These pages publish cumulative and weekly case counts, deaths, neuroinvasive disease counts, and county breakdowns. Targeting these domains directly maximizes the chance of retrieving the August 2024 weekly reports.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH or westnile.ca.gov weekly WNV surveillance summary page with tabular case counts by county and week
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official California state public health agency domain (.ca.gov); data attributed to CDPH Infectious Disease Branch or Vector-Borne Disease Section

query_batch.query: West Nile virus California August 2024 human cases neuroinvasive deaths county surveillance
query_batch.query_rationale: A broader web search using natural language terms likely to appear in CDPH press releases, county health department reports, and official surveillance summaries. 'Neuroinvasive' is the standard CDC/CDPH classification term for severe WNV disease and will help surface case-classification data. Avoids over-quoted exact phrases that may not match real page text.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH press release, county health department advisory, or westnile.ca.gov summary referencing August 2024 case counts
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Source attributed to CDPH, a California county public health department, or official state surveillance program

This provides a cross-validation source independent of CDPH and may include August 2024 cumulative figures.

query_batch.expected_trust_signal: CDC.gov domain; data labeled as ArboNET surveillance system output

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 returned strong signals from westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletins (weekly PDFs), CDC ArboNET historic data, and county-level sources. However, critical gaps remain: (1) The two Arbobulletin PDFs identified (week 29 and week 32) bracket August 2024 but their exact epidemiological week dates are not confirmed in the snippets — additional weekly bulletins covering weeks 31–35 (roughly August 2024) are needed to pin down August-specific cumulative case counts and deaths. (2) No deaths figure with an August 2024 date anchor has been confirmed for California specifically — the Placer County snippet mentions "54 confirmed cases and 5 deaths" but no date is confirmed. (3) The CIDRAP Facebook post references a 5th California WNV death but no date or county is confirmed. (4) Hospitalization data has not surfaced. (5) The westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletin download index page has not been directly targeted to enumerate all August 2024 weekly PDFs (weeks ~31–35). A second iteration targeting the Arbobulletin index, specific August-week bulletins, CDPH press releases with death/hospitalization data, and the CDC 2024 current-season statistics page will close these gaps within the 4-query cap.
